question: What is WebSQL?
answerGeneral: WebSQL was a browser API that exposed a relational (SQLite) database to client-side JavaScript, allowing SQL queries (`SELECT`, `INSERT`, etc.) in the browser. It was never standardised by W3C and was deprecated in 2010 because the spec was entirely bound to SQLite — violating the principle of having multiple independent implementations. All three major engines (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) never reached full agreement and Firefox never shipped it. It is now removed from Chrome 119+ and should not be used in new projects. The modern replacements are **IndexedDB** (complex structured data), **localStorage/sessionStorage** (simple key-value), and **OPFS** (Origin Private File System, for large binary data).
answerGeneralTr: WebSQL, istemci tarafı JavaScript'e ilişkisel (SQLite) bir veritabanı sunan, tarayıcıda SQL sorguları çalıştırmaya olanak tanıyan bir tarayıcı API'siydi. W3C tarafından hiçbir zaman standardize edilmedi ve 2010'da kullanımdan kaldırıldı çünkü spec tamamen SQLite'a bağlıydı. Modern alternatifler: **IndexedDB** (karmaşık yapılandırılmış veriler), **localStorage/sessionStorage** (basit anahtar-değer) ve **OPFS** (büyük ikili veriler).

question: What are Web Workers?
answerGeneral: Web Workers run JavaScript in a background thread, separate from the main UI thread. Because browsers are single-threaded, heavy computation (image processing, data parsing, cryptography) on the main thread blocks rendering and makes the UI unresponsive. Workers solve this by running the heavy task off-thread and communicating results back via `postMessage`. Workers have no access to the DOM, `window`, or `document` — they only share data via structured cloning (copies, not references). Types: **Dedicated Worker** (one page), **Shared Worker** (multiple pages, same origin), **Service Worker** (network proxy, offline support).
answerGeneralTr: Web Workers, JavaScript'i ana UI iş parçacığından ayrı bir arka plan iş parçacığında çalıştırır. Tarayıcılar tek iş parçacıklı olduğundan, ana iş parçacığındaki ağır hesaplamalar render'ı engeller ve UI'ı yanıt vermez hale getirir. Workers, ağır görevi iş parçacığı dışında çalıştırarak ve sonuçları `postMessage` aracılığıyla ileterek bunu çözer. Workers'ın DOM, `window` veya `document`'a erişimi yoktur. Türler: **Dedicated Worker** (tek sayfa), **Shared Worker** (birden çok sayfa), **Service Worker** (ağ proxy'si, çevrimdışı destek).

question: What is WebP?
answerGeneral: WebP is a modern image format developed by Google that provides superior lossless and lossy compression for web images compared to JPEG and PNG. Lossless WebP is 26% smaller than PNG; lossy WebP is 25–34% smaller than JPEG at equivalent visual quality. It also supports transparency (unlike JPEG) and animation (unlike JPEG/PNG). Browser support is now universal (all major browsers since 2020). Use `<picture>` with a WebP `<source>` and JPEG/PNG fallback for safe deployment. Next.js Image component serves WebP (or AVIF) automatically via its image optimisation pipeline.

For pre-built static assets, prefer AVIF. For runtime optimisation, Next.js and Cloudflare Images try AVIF first then fall back to WebP based on the `Accept` header.

question: What kind of things must you be wary of when designing or developing for multilingual sites?
answerGeneral: Key concerns: (1) **Text expansion** — translated text can be 30–100% longer than English, breaking fixed-width layouts; (2) **RTL layout** — Arabic, Hebrew, Persian require `dir="rtl"` and CSS `logical properties` (`margin-inline-start` instead of `margin-left`); (3) **Font support** — not all fonts include non-Latin glyphs; (4) **Date/number/currency formatting** — use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.NumberFormat`; (5) **Sorting and collation** — `Intl.Collator`; (6) **Pluralisation rules** — languages have different plural forms (Russian has three); (7) **Images with embedded text** — must be localised separately; (8) **SEO** — correct `hreflang` and `lang` attributes per locale.
answerGeneralTr: Temel endişeler: (1) **Metin genişlemesi** — çevrilmiş metin İngilizce'den %30-100 daha uzun olabilir, sabit genişlikli düzenleri bozar; (2) **RTL düzen** — Arapça, İbranice, Farsça `dir="rtl"` ve CSS mantıksal özellikleri gerektirir; (3) **Yazı tipi desteği** — tüm fontlar Latin olmayan glifleri içermez; (4) **Tarih/sayı/para birimi biçimlendirme** — `Intl.DateTimeFormat` ve `Intl.NumberFormat` kullanın; (5) **Çoğul kuralları** — dillerin farklı çoğul biçimleri vardır; (6) **Gömülü metinli görseller** — ayrı olarak yerelleştirilmeli; (7) **SEO** — her yerel için doğru `hreflang` ve `lang` öznitelikleri.

Buttonları, kartları ve nav öğelerini içerikle esnemek için tasarla. Çevrilmiş metni kesen sabit genişlikler ve `overflow: hidden` kullanmaktan kaçın.

question: What are the building blocks of HTML5?
answerGeneral: HTML5 is defined by several interconnected specs: (1) **HTML markup** — the element vocabulary (semantic, form, media elements); (2) **DOM API** — JavaScript interfaces to manipulate documents; (3) **CSS3** — styling (though a separate spec, always co-evolved); (4) **JavaScript / ECMAScript** — behaviour layer; (5) **Web APIs** — Canvas, WebGL, Web Workers, WebSocket, Geolocation, Web Storage, IndexedDB, Drag & Drop, History API, Notifications, File API; (6) **SVG and MathML** — embedded in HTML5 natively; (7) **Accessibility (ARIA)** — attributes for AT. Together these form the open web platform — a complete application runtime without plugins.
answerGeneralTr: HTML5, birbiriyle bağlantılı birkaç spec tarafından tanımlanır: (1) **HTML işaretlemesi** — öğe sözlüğü (anlamsal, form, medya öğeleri); (2) **DOM API** — belgeleri manipüle etmek için JavaScript arayüzleri; (3) **CSS3** — biçimlendirme; (4) **JavaScript/ECMAScript** — davranış katmanı; (5) **Web API'leri** — Canvas, WebGL, Web Workers, WebSocket, Geolocation, Web Storage, IndexedDB, History API; (6) **SVG ve MathML** — HTML5'te yerel olarak gömülü; (7) **Erişilebilirlik (ARIA)** — yardımcı teknolojiler için öznitelikler. Bunlar birlikte eklentisiz eksiksiz bir uygulama çalışma zamanı oluşturur.

question: What is the purpose of the <main> element?
answerGeneral: `<main>` identifies the dominant content of the `<body>` — the central topic of the document, excluding repeated site chrome like navigation, headers, footers, and sidebars. There must be only one visible `<main>` per page (multiple can exist if all but one are hidden with `hidden`). It carries the implicit ARIA role `main`, allowing screen reader users to jump directly to the primary content with a single keystroke (Skip to main content shortcut). It does not affect visual layout — its value is semantic and accessibility-driven.

question: Why would you use a srcset attribute in an image tag? Explain the process the browser uses when evaluating the content of this attribute.
answerGeneral: `srcset` lets you provide multiple image candidates at different resolutions or pixel densities so the browser selects the most appropriate one based on the device's screen size and pixel density, downloading only what's needed. Without `srcset`, a 4K retina display gets the same image as a basic phone — either too blurry or wasting bandwidth. The browser evaluates each candidate's width descriptor (`w`) against the `sizes` attribute (which defines the rendered width at each breakpoint) to compute the effective pixel density, then picks the closest match. Alternatively, the `x` descriptor serves different densities (1x, 2x) without size calculation.
detailMd: ## Width descriptors + sizes (recommended) ```html ``` ### Browser evaluation algorithm 1. **Parse `sizes`**: evaluate CSS media conditions top-to-bottom, find the first match, extract the declared width (e.g. `640px` on a 600px viewport) 2. **Account for DPR**: multiply declared width by `window.devicePixelRatio` (e.g. 640 × 2 = 1280 needed pixels) 3. **Select from `srcset`**: pick the candidate whose `w` is ≥ needed pixels — browser may pick larger for quality headroom 4. **Download**: fetch the chosen URL ## Pixel density descriptors (simpler) ```html ``` ## for art direction ```html ``` ## Next.js Image handles this automatically ```tsx ```

question: What is an HTML preprocessor and have you used one?
answerGeneral: An HTML preprocessor is a tool that compiles an extended markup language into standard HTML. Common examples: **Pug** (indentation-based, supports mixins, iteration, inheritance), **Haml**, **Slim**, and **Nunjucks**. They add features HTML lacks: variables, loops, partials/includes, template inheritance. In modern React/Next.js development, **JSX** serves the same purpose — it extends JavaScript with XML-like syntax that compiles to `React.createElement`. Server-side template engines like **Handlebars** or **EJS** are also preprocessors in the sense that they process templates at render time. The trend in frontend is away from dedicated HTML preprocessors towards JSX and framework-native solutions.

question: How would you select SVG or Canvas for your site?
answerGeneral: **SVG** is a retained-mode vector format: each shape is a DOM node, infinitely scalable, accessible (text is real text, ARIA works), searchable, and style-able with CSS. Best for: logos, icons, illustrations, charts with few elements, interactive diagrams where individual elements need events or animation. **Canvas** is an immediate-mode raster surface: you draw pixel commands and the library forgets the shape — no DOM nodes. Best for: games, real-time visualisations with thousands of elements (particle systems, large datasets), image processing, and WebGL 3D rendering. Rule of thumb: under ~1000 interactive elements → SVG; over ~1000 or real-time → Canvas/WebGL.
detailMd:
## SVG — retained mode

```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-label="Progress chart">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="none" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="8"
    stroke-dasharray="188" stroke-dashoffset="47" />
  <text x="50" y="55" text-anchor="middle" font-size="20">75%</text>
</svg>
```

- Each element is a real DOM node — `addEventListener`, CSS transitions, ARIA all work
- Scales perfectly to any resolution (vector math)
- Text is real text — selectable, searchable, screen-reader accessible
- Expensive with thousands of elements (each triggers layout)

## Canvas — immediate mode

```html
<canvas id="c" width="800" height="600"></canvas>
```

```js
const ctx = document.getElementById('c').getContext('2d');

// Draw 10,000 particles — Canvas handles this, SVG would choke
particles.forEach(p => {
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, p.r, 0, Math.PI * 2);
  ctx.fillStyle = p.color;
  ctx.fill();
});

// To update: clear and redraw everything
ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 800, 600);
```

- Pixels only — no DOM nodes, no events on individual shapes
- Hit-testing requires manual math
- Must redraw the entire scene every frame for animation
- Doesn't scale (raster) — use `devicePixelRatio` for sharp display

## Decision matrix

| Factor | SVG | Canvas |
|---|---|---|
| Element count | < ~1000 | > ~1000 |
| Accessibility needed | ✅ | ❌ (need workaround) |
| CSS animations | ✅ | ❌ |
| Hit-testing / events | Easy (DOM) | Manual |
| Image processing | ❌ | ✅ |
| 3D rendering | Limited | WebGL |
| Print quality | ✅ (vector) | Limited (raster) |

## Libraries

- **SVG**: D3.js (data-driven), Snap.svg, GSAP
- **Canvas 2D**: Konva, Fabric.js, p5.js
- **WebGL (Canvas 3D)**: Three.js, Babylon.js, PixiJS
answerGeneralTr: **SVG**, alıkonulmuş modlu bir vektör formatıdır: her şekil bir DOM düğümüdür, sonsuz ölçeklenebilir, erişilebilir (metin gerçek metindir, ARIA çalışır) ve CSS ile biçimlendirilebilir. En iyi kullanım: logolar, ikonlar, az elemanlı grafikler, bireysel öğelerin olaylar veya animasyon gerektirdiği etkileşimli diyagramlar. **Canvas**, anlık modlu bir raster yüzeydir: piksel komutları çizersiniz ve şekil unutulur — DOM düğümü yoktur. En iyi kullanım: oyunlar, binlerce elemanlı gerçek zamanlı görselleştirmeler. Kural: ~1000'den az etkileşimli öğe → SVG; ~1000'den fazla veya gerçek zamanlı → Canvas/WebGL.
detailMdTr:
## SVG — Alıkonulmuş Mod

```html
<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" aria-label="İlerleme grafiği">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="none" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="8"
    stroke-dasharray="188" stroke-dashoffset="47" />
  <text x="50" y="55" text-anchor="middle" font-size="20">%75</text>
</svg>
```

- Her öğe gerçek bir DOM düğümüdür — `addEventListener`, CSS geçişleri, ARIA hepsi çalışır
- Herhangi bir çözünürlüğe mükemmel ölçeklenir (vektör matematiği)
- Metin gerçek metindir — seçilebilir, aranabilir, ekran okuyucu erişilebilir
- Binlerce öğeyle pahalıdır (her biri düzeni tetikler)

## Canvas — Anlık Mod

```html
<canvas id="c" width="800" height="600"></canvas>
```

```js
const ctx = document.getElementById('c').getContext('2d');

// 10.000 parçacık çiz — Canvas bunu halleder, SVG tıkanır
partikuller.forEach(p => {
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, p.r, 0, Math.PI * 2);
  ctx.fillStyle = p.renk;
  ctx.fill();
});

// Güncellemek için: temizle ve her şeyi yeniden çiz
ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 800, 600);
```

- Yalnızca piksel — DOM düğümü yok, bireysel şekillerde olay yok
- İsabet testi manuel matematik gerektirir

## Karar Matrisi

| Faktör | SVG | Canvas |
|---|---|---|
| Öğe sayısı | < ~1000 | > ~1000 |
| Erişilebilirlik gerekli | ✅ | ❌ |
| CSS animasyonları | ✅ | ❌ |
| Görüntü işleme | ❌ | ✅ |
| 3D render | Sınırlı | WebGL |

## Kütüphaneler

- **SVG**: D3.js, Snap.svg, GSAP
- **Canvas 2D**: Konva, Fabric.js, p5.js
- **WebGL**: Three.js, Babylon.js, PixiJS
